title: Lens Numericals — Solving Strategies
notes: Part 1: Question Types & Their Solving Approaches
Every mirror problem falls into one of three main categories.
Type 1: The "Direct Finder"
What it is: The question gives you two variables (like u and f) and asks you to find the third (v), or asks for the final magnification.

Solving Approach: Write down the givens with correct signs. Use the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u to find the missing distance. Use the magnification formula (m = −v/u or m = v/u) to find the image characteristics.
Type 2: The "Magnification Pivot"
What it is: The question gives you the focal length (or radius) and says the image is "n times magnified," but does not give you v.

Solving Approach: Express v in terms of u using the magnification formula (e.g., v = 3u or v = −3u). Substitute this expression into the mirror formula so that u is the only unknown variable. Crucial: if the question does not specify if the image is real or virtual, you must solve for both cases separately.
Type 3: The "Two-Position Shift"
What it is: The object is placed at one position, then moved to a second position.

Solving Approach: Step 1 (First Position) — use the first set of data to find the focal length (f) of the mirror; the mirror doesn't change, so f stays constant. Step 2 (Second Position) — use the newly found f along with the new position data to solve for the final target.
Part 2: The Hint Decoder (What Indicates What)
When reading a physics problem, specific words act as hidden codes.
1. Hints about the Mirror Type
"Shaving mirror" or "Makeup mirror" → It is a Concave mirror used to create an enlarged, virtual image.
"Rear-view mirror" or "Driver's mirror" → It is a Convex mirror used to see a wide view of smaller, virtual images.
"Reflecting surface is curved inwards" → Concave mirror.
"Reflecting surface is curved outwards" → Convex mirror.
2. Hints about Image Nature & Sign Rules

The Phrase in the QuestionStandard CartesianReal-is-Positive (RIP)
"Brought to a focus on a screen"Real Image → v negative, m negativeReal Image → v positive, m positive
"Inverted image"Real Image → v negative, m negativeReal Image → v positive, m positive
"Erect image" or "Upright"Virtual Image → v positive, m positiveVirtual Image → v negative, m negative
"Formed behind the mirror"Virtual Image → v positive, m positiveVirtual Image → v negative, m negative
"Formed in front of the mirror"Real Image → v negative, m negativeReal Image → v positive, m positive
Step 1: Find the Image Nature from the Keywords

If the question says......the Nature of the Image is
"Erect", "Upright", or "Behind the mirror"Virtual
"Inverted", "On a screen", or "In front of a concave mirror"Real
"Convex mirror" (for any real object)Always Virtual (and smaller)
"Magnified image by a convex mirror"Trick question! Convex mirrors cannot magnify
"Diminished image by a concave mirror"Always Real
Step 2: Choose the Sign Based on Your Convention
Option A: Standard Cartesian Convention (Most Common)
Real Image: Image is upside down (inverted) → take magnification as negative (−m). Image is in front of the mirror → take image distance as negative (−v).
Virtual Image: Image is upright (erect) → take magnification as positive (+m). Image is behind the mirror → take image distance as positive (+v).
Option B: Real-is-Positive (RIP) System
Real Image: real things get a plus sign → take magnification as positive (+m). Image is real → take image distance as positive (+v).
Virtual Image: virtual things get a minus sign → take magnification as negative (−m). Image is virtual → take image distance as negative (−v).
A Quick Example to Clarify
Question: "A concave mirror forms an image magnified 3 times on a screen."
1. Find Nature: the keyword "on a screen" means the image must be Real.
2. Apply Sign: In Standard Cartesian, take m = −3. In Real-is-Positive, take m = +3.
